title: RISE Live: catalog words
acceptance: During a reading, words asked in the bar (typed, or heard and asked with Enter) that are nothing but one of RISE's own visuals are answered by the venue with no model call: the visual is shown, the reading is taken up again at once, no request is opened or counted, and the bar says what is shown in plain catalog words for about 4 seconds ("Showing the attractor.", "Making the attractor calmer.").

The recogniser (src/live/catalog-words.js) is pure and draws its vocabulary from the manifests (engine ids, parameter values, cues) plus one small alias table: fractal flame and flame (living flame), pendulum(s) (harmonograph), swarm and filament (attractor trace), rotary (harmonograph pendulums), calmer, brighter, warmer, cooler (cues); a system or palette sets that parameter beside its engine; only the closed filler list may surround them. Anything else, two engines or cues, a value without its engine, a cue the engine on screen does not take, still or oracle, and any input over 120 characters is null and goes to the model unchanged; matching is case-insensitive and folds accents and full-width letters.

Before a reading and after one, every question goes to RISE as before; a reading the runtime cannot show it in (no room for another scene, a cue the engine on screen does not take) sends the words to the model as an interjection.

An engine is shown through the runtime's existing picture path (withPictures, withPictureClips) from the phrase on screen, so the journal, the three frames and perception see it; a cue goes through the running engine's own control.

The hold protects the reader's choice from the model's pre-planned changes, not from the reader's own later requests: from the passage it was chosen in, no beat starts or cues a scene and the model's @visual, @cue, @illustrate and pictures not yet shown are held and journalled as room.held; when the reader then asks RISE something inside the reading, the hold ends where that answer is first heard and the answer's scenes, changes and pictures apply; a new catalog choice starts a new hold; the next question, a new reading, holds nothing. Looks and paces are not held.

Perception carries the request and the hold to the next request: chose { engine, values?, cue? } and withheld { by: 'rise' }, admitted by admitPerception with bounds (an engine the venue shows by name, at most four of its own values, one of its cues), said as "asked for the attractor (swarm), and it was shown at once" and "RISE’s own scene changes after that were held", and explained in Live's perception guide. The beat grammar, the Current schema, the Worker, the host guide and the Composer card are unchanged.

evidence.note: §25 Catalog words: the recogniser, where it is asked, how it is shown, the precedence rule, what the next request is told, and what is not verified.

Command: npx vitest run src/live/catalog-words.test.js src/live/runtime.catalog.test.js src/live/perception.test.js src/live/host/venue.test.js src/live/adapters/openai-instructions.test.js. Branch live-catalog-words, written first and watched failing: catalog-words 16, runtime.catalog 10 (after review: the reader's later question ends the hold, a new choice holds again, and an answer naming one of RISE's engines before its first beat is grafted, a latent STREAM_ENDED fixed in takeAnswer), perception 36, venue 61, openai-instructions 35, all passed. npx vitest run src/live: 1994 passed, 1 failed (runtime.seek 'lists every passage in order' fails on origin/main af117d0b as well). Tests importing core/beats.js (8 files) 196 passed.

Command: npx playwright test e2e/live.spec.js -g "catalog words". 1 passed (46.1 s) on the demo provider: 'attractor' typed while the figure holds the full frame shows the attractor in the outer shell, the bar says 'Showing the attractor.', no interjection request is journalled and the demo's later disk scene is held. With the venue's wiring removed the same test fails (note empty).

PR #660 on branch live-catalog-words: the hold ends at the reader's own later question (review), a Codex finding answered (Fixed in 431d72e8 by claude[bot]: a held beat cue is journalled; covered by a test in 84c301a0), CI green on feebf55c. Squash-merged as 8df83ce7; deployed in release b48ef88e (release.txt b48ef88e35db, 2026-10-13), which contains it. Not accepted by a human.

Production check on release b48ef88e, headless Chromium at 1440x900, the demo reading: 'attractor' typed while the figure held the full frame; the frame went from full to shell with the attractor open in it, the bar read 'Showing the attractor.', one visual.chosen and no interjection.asked in the journal, no page errors. Screenshots kept locally (prod-words-1440x900.png, prod-words-1440x900-note.png). A scripted check, not a human acceptance.

Branch live-ask-bar-bottom (LIVE-030): a catalog word's note ("Showing the attractor.") now stays until the visual it named is on screen and the room's frame has opened onto it (frames.js director settled(), on the venue's clock), then 1.5 s more; under reduced motion, and with no frames to follow, 1.5 s after the switch. Before, it went after a fixed 4 s, while a change from the full frame to the shell takes about 5 s. Local: npx vitest run src/live/host/frames.test.js src/live/host/venue.test.js, 97 passed (the director at rest, the note through a shell-to-full change and 1.4 s after it, gone at 1.6 s; reduced motion 1.5 s); npx playwright test e2e/live.spec.js -g "catalog words" passed within the targeted set of 16 (the note still shown once the shell is open on the attractor, gone within 3 s). Not merged, deployed or accepted by a human.

Branch live-catalog-frame-switch, commit c5ad86c6: a catalog word typed while held now reaches the screen at once. Cause: the chosen engine was placed on the phrase already on screen, but the visual schedule takes a cue only when the Player shows an atom, so the change waited for the next phrase (genesis and fractal under the attractor: the shell and the attractor stayed seconds, 12 s on one measured run; every engine alike). Fix: src/core/visual-scheduler.js extend shows the atom on screen the cue the longer program gives it. Local: npx vitest run src/live/runtime.catalog.test.js, 21 passed (10 new, one per named engine: attractor, genesis, living-flame, fractal, turrell, neural, rockgarden, harmonograph, ostensoria, apparitio, chosen in a 9 s hold; cue on screen within 50 ms, the frame open and at rest within the two frames transition times; all 10 failed before the fix); src/core/visual-scheduler.test.js 17 passed; npx playwright test e2e/live.spec.js -g "catalog words" passed with genesis from the shell reaching the full frame within 2.5 s (failed before the fix: frame stayed shell). Not merged, deployed or accepted by a human.

Branch catalog-note-names, code at f9df3a05: the bar's note names each engine as the Reader's catalog does, a proper name without "the" (Genesis, Turrell Fields, Ostensoria, Apparitio) and a common noun with it (the attractor, the harmonograph, the fractal, the living flame, the rock garden, the neural network); the same names go up with the reader's next words. Local: catalog-words every-engine note test (red before), catalog-words importers 3 files 109 passed, venue tests, fast set 125 files, e2e catalog words passed; ci-hygiene, vite build, first load within budget. Not merged yet; not accepted by a human.

summary: In RISE Live, a reader who names one of RISE's own visuals during a reading gets it at once, with no model call; RISE's own scene changes after it in that reading are held, and the next request is told.
